JEE Main 2027 registration numbers climb
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency reports 786,687 submitted applications for JEE Main 2027. Of those, 594,259 candidates have completed the required fee payment. The deadline to register without a late fee is November 22. Roughly one in four applicants has yet to settle the bill.

stories.title: NTA sets November 22 deadline for JEE Main 2027
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has opened registration for JEE Main 2027 Session 1. Applications must be submitted via the MeriPehchan platform by November 22. Candidates are required to provide personal and academic details, upload documentation, and pay the application fee to finalize their entry.

stories.title: Nearly 800,000 apply for JEE Main January session
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has received 786,687 applications for the upcoming JEE Main 2027 session. Candidates have until November 22 to complete their registration and fee payments. The agency continues to process submissions ahead of the final deadline for the January examination.

NTA reports 7.86 lakh JEE Main applications
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has recorded 786,687 applications for JEE Main 2027 Session 1. As of November 14, 594,259 candidates have completed their fee payments. The window to register without incurring a late fee remains open until November 22.

stories.title: JEE Main 2027 registration data released
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency reports 786,687 total registrations for JEE Main 2027, with 594,259 candidates having paid the examination fee. The deadline to apply without a late fee is November 22, with a late-fee extension available until November 26. Corrections open on November 27.

stories.title: NTA clarifies category selection for JEE Main 2027
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has issued guidance on application categories for JEE Main 2027. The instructions specify how candidates should select their status based on citizenship and Aadhaar documentation. The clarification applies to both Indian citizens and Non-Resident Indians preparing for the Session 1 examination.

Germany launches online student visa portal
stories.summary: The German Embassy in Dhaka has introduced a digital application system for national student visas. The new portal replaces the previous appointment waiting list. All applicants, including those previously registered, must now submit fresh applications through the German Federal Foreign Office portal.

Irish universities report €8 million loss from visa refusals
stories.summary: Irish universities report losing over €8 million this academic year due to an increase in international student visa refusals. The Technological University Association expects sector-wide losses to exceed €5 million for 2027. Institutions cite these funding gaps as a challenge to maintaining financial sustainability.

stories.title: Canada targets 150,000 international students for 2027
stories.summary: Canada has set an annual target of 150,000 new international student arrivals for 2027 through 2029. The move is part of a new Immigration Levels Plan aimed at tightening temporary immigration controls. Indian applicants remain eligible to apply under the national cap.

stories.title: US international student interest rises 40 percent
stories.summary: International student interest in US study programs rose 40 percent in the week following the November 3 midterm elections, according to Studyportals. The data suggests a potential recovery after two years of declining demand. The shift in interest followed Democratic victories in the House and Senate.

stories.title: Canada extends international student intake cap until 2029
stories.summary: Canada has retained its annual target of 1.5 lakh new international student arrivals for the next three years. The decision is part of the 2027-2029 Immigration Levels Plan, which also sets targets for temporary foreign workers. The country plans to host 3.7 lakh temporary residents annually through 2029.

stories.title: German embassy to launch digital student visa portal in January
stories.summary: The German Embassy in Dhaka will introduce a digital application system for student visas on 1 January. Applicants for bachelor and master studies must use the government's Auslandsportal to submit forms and upload documents. The embassy aims to increase transparency and reduce appointment wait times for prospective students.

stories.title: German embassy to launch digital student visa application system for Bangladeshis in January
stories.summary: The German Embassy in Dhaka will introduce a digital application system for student visas on 1 January. Applicants will use the government's Auslandsportal to submit forms and documents, with VFS conducting a preliminary review. The embassy aims to simplify the process and reduce appointment wait times for students.

Applications open for 1,000 Commonwealth teaching scholarships
stories.summary: The Australian Government has opened the fourth round of its Commonwealth Teaching Scholarship program, offering up to $40,000 for undergraduate or $20,000 for postgraduate studies. The program aims to deliver 5,000 scholarships over five years. The government described the first three rounds as a big success.

stories.title: CUHK opens applications for fully funded PhD fellowships
stories.summary: The Chinese University of Hong Kong has opened applications for its 2027-28 PhD Fellowship Scheme. The university offers scholarship packages exceeding US$232,420, alongside faculty mentorship and research facilities. The institution describes itself as an ideal launchpad for high-achieving international scholars to drive global impact.

stories.title: New Zealand government opens scholarship applications
stories.summary: The New Zealand government is accepting applications for its Manaaki scholarship programme for international students. The scheme provides fully funded undergraduate, postgraduate and short-term training opportunities. Administered by Education New Zealand, the programme aims to strengthen partnerships with developing countries through investment in education and leadership.

stories.title: University of Edinburgh offers two fully funded PhD studentships
stories.summary: The University of Edinburgh has invited applications for two doctoral studentships in law and related subjects for the 2027-2028 academic year. Selected scholars will receive tuition coverage and an annual stipend of approximately £21,805 for up to three years, provided they maintain satisfactory academic progress.

stories.title: Columbia Law School opens human rights fellowship applications
stories.summary: Columbia Law School is accepting applications for its 2027-2028 Human Rights LL.M. Fellowship. The programme provides tuition assistance and access to the university's Human Rights Institute for graduates pursuing careers in advocacy or academia. Fellows also receive academic mentoring and professional development opportunities throughout the year.

stories.title: Harvard Law School opens LL.M. financial aid applications
stories.summary: Harvard Law School has opened applications for need-based financial aid for its 2027-2028 LL.M. programme. Assistance includes scholarships and loans, with a small number of grants covering full tuition and partial living expenses for students demonstrating serious financial need. Applications are open to international law graduates.

stories.title: University of Cambridge invites PhD in Law applications
stories.summary: The University of Cambridge has opened applications for its 2027-2028 PhD in Law programme. Funding is available through the Cambridge Trust, Gates Cambridge and individual colleges. Awards range from full coverage of tuition and living expenses to partial financial assistance for successful doctoral research candidates.

stories.title: University of Edinburgh offers LL.M. research scholarships
stories.summary: The Edinburgh Legal Education Trust is offering scholarships for LL.M. by Research students in Scots private law for 2027-2028. Full-time students may receive tuition coverage at the home-student rate and a maintenance grant of £21,805. The programme is open to international law graduates.

stories.title: World Food Programme opens 2026 paid positions
stories.summary: The United Nations World Food Programme is offering paid positions for university students and recent graduates in Egypt, Italy and Sierra Leone. Participants receive up to $1,000 monthly to gain experience in humanitarian and international development sectors. The programme focuses on initiatives addressing global hunger and food insecurity.

stories.title: Ministry of Tribal Affairs opens scholarship applications
stories.summary: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs has invited applications for its 2026-27 scholarship scheme for Scheduled Tribe students. Selected candidates receive tuition support and an annual stipend of ₹36,000. The scheme covers undergraduate and postgraduate courses, including those at National Law Universities, for eligible students across India.

stories.title: UGC invites applications for Ishan Uday scholarships
stories.summary: The University Grants Commission is accepting applications for the 2026-27 Ishan Uday scholarship for students from North Eastern India. The scheme provides ₹8,000 per month for ten months, totaling ₹80,000 annually. Approximately 10,000 scholarships are available for students pursuing undergraduate degrees and professional programmes.

stories.title: University of Leeds offers three PhD scholarships
stories.summary: The University of Leeds is offering three doctoral scholarships for the 2027 academic year in performance and cultural industries. The awards provide full tuition fees and a £21,805 annual stipend. The funding is open to both UK and international candidates.

stories.title: UNSW Sydney reports momentum
stories.summary: UNSW Sydney vice chancellor Attila Brungs says there is a palpable sense of excitement on campus. He describes 2026 as an extraordinary year for the institution. When the university starts to get momentum, people feel it, according to the vice chancellor.

stories.title: University funding and performance
stories.summary: Australian universities rely on a mix of Commonwealth government funding, international student fees, and research grants. The sector maintains that high performance requires consistent funding. The diversity of these revenue streams is considered essential for effective reporting about outcomes.

stories.title: University of Melbourne startup develops brain-to-text device
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Melbourne have spun out a startup called Fluent to develop a device that translates brain activity into text. The implant sits under the scalp to assist people with neurological disorders. It functions similarly to a cochlear implant.

Water Resources University rises in rankings
stories.summary: Water Resources University climbed 315 places in the 2027 QS Asia Rankings, landing in the 731 to 740 group. Rector Nguyen Trung Viet attributed the jump to improvements in research, international publications, and faculty quality. The university was previously ranked significantly lower among the 1,722 institutions surveyed.

stories.title: B.C. universities rank for graduate employability
stories.summary: The 2027 Global Employability University Ranking and Survey places the University of British Columbia third among Canadian institutions and 33rd globally. Unlike academic-focused lists, this survey relies on employer assessments of which schools produce the most employable graduates.

stories.title: UK universities assessed in global rankings
stories.summary: The Times Higher Education World University Rankings have assessed data from over 3,000 universities to identify the top institutions in the UK. The rankings serve as a comprehensive assessment of global research performance and academic standing.

stories.title: HEC urges Pakistani universities to join rankings
stories.summary: The Higher Education Commission has requested that public and private universities in Pakistan participate in the QS World University Rankings 2028. Executive Director Zia Ul Haq noted that while some institutions have performed well, overall participation remains limited. Universities are advised to submit data by the deadline.

stories.title: India invites Singaporean universities to establish campuses
stories.summary: India has invited Singaporean universities to open campuses and help develop university townships. The proposal draws on the National University of Singapore's University Town model. Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi discussed the potential for deeper cooperation in research and innovation with his Singaporean counterpart.

stories.title: UMass Lowell named top public value school
stories.summary: U.S. News & World Report has ranked UMass Lowell as the top public university in Massachusetts for value. The school moved up nine spots to 83rd nationally. The designation evaluates institutions based on a combination of academic quality and affordability for undergraduate students.

stories.title: Sogang University integrates AI into global strategy
stories.summary: Sogang University president Sim Jong-hyeok is focusing on interdisciplinary AI and personalized education to increase the school's global impact. The university also emphasizes relationship-building between international students and faculty, including through group hiking trips, to support campus life.

stories.title: U.S. university rankings show varied results
stories.summary: MIT leads in both Forbes and QS rankings, while Harvard holds the top spot on the Academic Ranking of World Universities. Sixteen U.S. schools appear in the top 25 across all three lists. Rankings often differ significantly, such as Princeton placing second in Forbes but 11th in QS.

stories.title: Search underway for missing student in Panchkula
stories.summary: A six-year-old student went missing after being dropped off at her school in Haryana’s Panchkula district on October 28. The child was not present when her driver arrived for pickup, and her bag was found at the school reception. Authorities are investigating the incident.

stories.title: AYUSH colleges protest licensing exam requirements
stories.summary: AYUSH colleges in Madhya Pradesh are opposing the mandatory National Exit Test for graduates. They argue that requiring an additional licensing exam for traditional medicine students, while MBBS students only take the NEET UG, constitutes unfair treatment. The colleges have written to the national regulatory commission.

stories.title: Universities pivot to adaptability for AI era
stories.summary: University leaders are emphasizing flexibility as artificial intelligence threatens to disrupt traditional career paths. UNSW Sydney deputy vice chancellor Sarah Maddison suggests that because the future impact of AI remains unknown, institutions should focus on core capabilities and attributes rather than specific discipline skills.

stories.title: Bond University integrates Indigenous teaching methods
stories.summary: Bond University has topped the teaching category in the Financial Review Best Universities list. Provost Keitha Dunstan attributes the success to embedding Indigenous ways of knowing and doing. The approach mirrors traditional yarning, which Dunstan describes as a fundamental method for learning and teaching.

stories.title: CQU monitors student engagement with frequent contact
stories.summary: Central Queensland University maintains a policy of frequent communication with students from equity backgrounds who show signs of disengagement. The process includes multiple emails and phone calls to offer advocacy or academic assistance. The university describes the effort as stopping short of harassment.

stories.title: Survey finds Indian students match global entrepreneurship rates
stories.summary: A survey by IIT Mandi and REVA University reports that 22 percent of Indian college students have launched businesses, matching the global average. Additionally, 43 percent of respondents expressed an interest in future entrepreneurship. The study involved a national sample of students.

stories.title: UGC proposes committee to reform agricultural university admissions
stories.summary: The University Grants Commission has proposed a committee of vice-chancellors to reform the agricultural cluster admission system. The goal is to fill all first-year seats and maintain the academic calendar. The committee will focus on improving test quality and reducing delays in the current admission process.

stories.title: UGC plans agricultural cluster admission reforms for 2027
stories.summary: The University Grants Commission plans to reform the agricultural cluster admission system starting in the 2027-28 academic year. The initiative aims to ensure all seats are filled and academic schedules are met. Ten universities are involved in the process of reviewing current admission tests and procedures.

stories.title: UGC plans reform of agricultural university admission tests from 2027-28 - Daily Sun
UGC considers creative questions for agricultural cluster tests
stories.summary: The University Grants Commission is looking to reform agricultural cluster admissions to fill seats and meet academic deadlines. Chairman Mamun Ahmed proposed a committee to improve test quality and assess student merit through creative questions. The committee will recommend measures to ensure all available seats are filled.

stories.title: Dhaka University issues admission guidelines for 2026-27
stories.summary: Dhaka University has opened applications for its 2026-27 undergraduate programmes, with the process closing on 25 November. The university has released six guidelines for applicants and provided instructions for students awaiting HSC re-evaluation results. Applications are open for five distinct academic units.

stories.title: BITS Pilani endowment fund reaches 54 million dollars
stories.summary: BITS Pilani has raised 54 million dollars for its endowment fund in 23 months, moving toward a 100 million dollar target. Annual alumni giving reached 82 crore rupees in the 2025-26 financial year. The institution notes this is 90 times the level recorded when the office was established.
